`Servex/ext/refine/test/live-refine-measure.mjs:113` escapes the backticks around `MIN_BATCH` and `MAX_WAIT_MS` inside the summary template literal. The unescaped ones closed the template early, which was a parse error, so the fix is correct and minimal. The other backticks in that template (lines 97-99) were already escaped.
I did not run `node --check` on the file. Run it once to confirm that line 113 was the only parse break.

`review/diff.patch` is the wrong diff: it only appends log lines to `sessions/2026/10/12/session-4e965597/servex-health/task.jsonl` and never touches `Servex/ext/refine/test/live-refine-measure.mjs`, so the review packet does not show the fix being reviewed. Regenerate it from commit cc9e89b7d.
`requirements.md` does not exist in refine-parse-fix/; the ask is only the one-line request in `task.jsonl` line 1 ("Servex restart refused: live-refine-measure.mjs does not parse").
Outside the packet, `node --check Servex/ext/refine/test/live-refine-measure.mjs` passes now, and cc9e89b7d is the commit that fixed it by escaping backticks. The actual fix looks fine and minimal.

`review/diff.patch` is the wrong diff for this task: it changes only `.claude/hooks/step-prompt.mjs:11-13` and never touches `Servex/ext/refine/test/live-refine-measure.mjs`, which is the file the ask (task.jsonl line 1) names. Regenerate the packet from the commit that escaped the backticks (cc9e89b7d), or move the hook change to its own task.
`requirements.md` does not exist in `refine-parse-fix/`, so "met?" could only be judged against the one-line request in `task.jsonl` line 1.

The hook change itself is small and reasonable: it prefers the real path that `append.mjs` prints (`<target>: appended`, `append.mjs:68`) and falls back to the old regex. It only helps if `step-prompt.mjs` runs as a PostToolUse hook, since `tool_response` is absent before the tool runs. Check the hook's registration in settings.
The new regex `^(.*task\.jsonl): appended` is greedy and anchored per line. A path containing spaces works, but a multi-file append prints one line per target and only the first is used.
